youtube.title: MONEY TALKS
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with Louis Boulanger about rising global debt and the growing cost of servicing it. They discuss the US national debt exceeding $40 trillion, weakening foreign demand for US Treasuries and the growing role of gold in central-bank reserves. Boulanger warns a global sovereign debt crisis may be emerging, and examines the potential impact on inflation, interest rates, currencies and households, including Japan’s debt and the yen carry trade. DISCLAIMER : The views and information shared on this show are for educational and informational purposes only. They do not constitute personalised financial, investment, tax, or legal advice. Listeners should seek guidance from a licensed financial professional who can provide advice based on their individual situation. Discover more from Louis at LB Now Tired of headlines telling you what to think? Think for yourself. Get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: FREDDIE PONTON
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan talks with 21st Century Wire's Freddie Ponton about Iran expanding its control over waters far beyond the Strait of Hormuz, disabling unauthorised vessels and warning any US allies joining the blockade will become targets. They also discuss Itamar Ben-Gvir's campaign centred on removing Gaza's population, which awaits US approval, and the Witkoff-Kushner meeting with Putin, where no territorial concessions were offered despite a temporary halt to strikes on Kyiv. Discover more from 21st Century Wire or find them on X Follow Freddie on X Editorial Note This interview presents the perspective of the guest and includes statements about highly contested events and issues relating to Israel and Gaza. Some of those statements are disputed and remain the subject of significant factual, legal and political disagreement. RCR publishes a range of perspectives on contentious issues and encourages listeners to consider the discussion critically and alongside other viewpoints. youtube.title: BOTH BARRELS
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke and Rachel Stewart host the Free Speech Union's Jillaine Heather and Stephen Franks for a debate on where free speech principles should apply. They clash over Rainbow Story Hour in libraries, with Stewart arguing children cannot meaningfully consent while Franks and Heather defend viewpoint-neutral access to public venues. The panel also examines Brian Tamaki's firearms licence revocation and whether New Zealand's “fit and proper person” test risks becoming a tool for political suppression.
